alex: Quick share — ran a 2h A/B comparing the new kernel-picker tweak (v2) vs v1 on replayed burst traffic (8xA100).

alex: TL;DR: v2 ups throughput but worsens tail. Baseline v1 p95=92ms p99=240ms avg=48ms throughput=135 req/s. v2 p95=110ms p99=310ms avg=60ms throughput=155 req/s.

maria: Huh. What changed in batching heuristics? microbatch sizing / wait windows?

alex: v1: max_batch_tokens=4096, max_wait_ms=8. v2: max_batch_tokens=8192, max_wait_ms=6 (we increased token cap, lowered wait to reduce avg queue).

jin: Lowering wait explains the higher throughput + worse tail (more small microbatches -> more kernel switches and overhead). KV cache behavior?

alex: KV hit rate roughly same (~76%). But profiling shows more small kernel launches on v2. kernel_switch_count/sec +22%.

sam: Can you paste the top perf counters from the run?

alex: ```
kernel_switches: 22k -> 27k
avg_tokens_per_batch: 18 -> 12
avg_queue_ms: 4.2 -> 3.1
cpu->gpu memcpy_count: +18%
```

maria: Seems like we traded queueing latency for increased dispatch/launch overhead. That will blow up p99. For SLOs maybe try raising max_wait_ms to 10 and lower max_batch_tokens to 6144 so batches can form but token cap prevents extreme batching latency.

jin: Also consider a kernel-affinity rule: prefer the fast matmul kernel only when seq_len>512 or tokens_per_batch>15, otherwise prefer cheaper single-kernel path. Avoids fallback thrash for small batches.

ops-bot: Deploy note: rolled canary v2 -> 10% traffic at 2024-06-12T15:30:00Z (rollback window 30m).

alex: I captured a tailtrace id tt-20240612-09. Logs show fallback kernel spikes aligning with KV eviction bursts.

sam: Patch idea: dynamic wait bump — when kv_miss_rate > 5% for >200ms, temporary bump max_wait_ms by +6ms for 1s to allow coalescing and reduce kernel_switch churn.

maria: I like the dynamic approach. Combine with jin's kernel-affinity rule. @jin can you own the canary + perf probes tomorrow?

jin: Yep. I'll add metrics: kernel_switches histogram, avg_tokens_per_batch gauge, and a p99-by-kernel dashboard. Also adding a microburst replay test in CI to catch regressions.

alex: SG. Saving artifacts to s3://redwood-perf/tt-20240612 and will add p95/p99 per-kernel to the console dashboard. :thumbsup:

maria: Follow-ups: (1) run 1h canary with dynamic wait + kernel-affinity, (2) collect KV eviction correlation, (3) perf CI job to run microburst replay nightly.

alex: Thanks all — keeping this thread for the rollout notes and quick triage.
